description: Citizenship in the Community looks at how local government, services and volunteers shape the place you live, and asks you to take part: attending a public meeting, interviewing someone in local government, volunteering, and presenting what you learned about your community.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)
Citizenship in the Community Digital Resource Guide (scouting.org)

requirements.title: What community citizenship means
requirements.summary: What good citizenship in your community means, its rights, duties and obligations, and how you can show it.

requirements.title: Mapping your community
requirements.summary: One of two options for exploring your community’s services, landmarks and resources.

children.title: Option A
children.summary: Mapping community services and landmarks and their distances from your home.

children.title: Option B
children.summary: The alternative exploration option described in the official requirement.

requirements.title: A public meeting
requirements.summary: Attending an approved local government or court meeting and analyzing an issue discussed there.

children.title: Attend the meeting
children.summary: Attending an approved in-person local government or court meeting.

children.title: An issue with different views
children.summary: Explaining an issue from the meeting where opinions differed and which view you favor.

requirements.title: Investigating a community issue
requirements.summary: Choosing a local issue, learning which part of local government handles it, and interviewing someone involved.

children.title: Who handles it
children.summary: Identifying which branch or office of local government deals with the issue.

children.title: Interview
children.summary: Interviewing someone from that office, with approval.

children.title: Sharing what you learned
children.summary: Sharing what you learned with your counselor.

requirements.title: A film about community service
requirements.summary: Watching an approved film about people who improved their community and discussing its lessons.

requirements.title: Taxpayer-funded services
requirements.summary: Community services paid for by taxes and why they matter.

requirements.title: Charity and volunteering
requirements.summary: Researching charitable organizations, choosing one, and volunteering with it for the required time.

children.title: Three organizations
children.summary: Identifying charitable organizations outside Scouting that serve your community.

children.title: Volunteering
children.summary: Learning how young people can help and volunteering with the organization, then discussing the experience.

requirements.title: Community presentation
requirements.summary: Preparing and giving a presentation about your community’s history, culture, strengths and challenges.
